title: Release Train - Weekly Prep & Go/No-Go Checklist (Luke Wu)
content:
Weekly release-train prep notes - quick personal scratchpad before sync (aim: capture go/no-go state, owners, and follow-ups)

Meeting: Release Train Weekly - Thu 10:00am
Attendees (expected): Release Train leads, SRE, Serving Runtime, Console, Product PM

High-level target: Ship v1.12.0 to hosted API + dedicated pools next week (soft rollout -> canary -> gradual promo).

Agenda (prep):
- Status overview: release branch, blocker list, CI green? (5m)
- Go/No-Go checklist review (15m)
- Canary plan & metrics (10m)
- Rollback criteria & runbook refresh (5m)
- Outstanding risks + mitigations (10m)
- Owners & action items (5m)

Go/No-Go checklist (quick status, owner, notes)
1) CI/Pipeline green for release branch - Owner: Samir Patel - STATUS: OK
   - All unit/integration tests passed on linux-gpu and ci-emulator. E2E flaky test (session-reconnect) re-run passed.
2) Infra capacity reserved for canary + promo - Owner: Olivia Martin - STATUS: PENDING
   - Need final commit for dedicated pool autoscale limits (JIRA:INF-330). Olivia to confirm quota by EOD Fri.
3) Canary traffic routing & feature flags ready - Owner: Maya Singh - STATUS: OK
   - Feature flag toggles prepared, helm charts updated. Canary will start at 1% traffic for 24h.
4) DB/migration scripts reviewed and runbook validated - Owner: Evan Ramirez - STATUS: BLOCKED
   - Migration REL-452 has a precondition (kv schema bump) that is still waiting validation in staging. Blocker until validated.
5) Performance/regression checks (latency, p95, token throughput) - Owner: Release QA (Samir backup) - STATUS: PENDING
   - Baseline run scheduled tonight; need comparison to last-prod for p95 and tail latency.
6) Observability & alerting (dashboards, SLOs, alert thresholds) - Owner: SRE oncall - STATUS: OK
   - New error budget burn dashboard added; paging rule updated for high kv-cache misses.
7) Security/keys/KMS reviewed for private deployments - Owner: Security team (noted) - STATUS: OK
   - No new key rotations required for this release.
8) Rollback plan & automated rollback tested - Owner: Release Engineer - STATUS: PENDING
   - Automated rollback script exists but not exercised against canary in the last month. Need a dry-run in staging.

Major blockers (items that could force no-go):
- Migration REL-452 validation failing in staging (Evan) - HIGH priority. If not validated by Fri noon, escalate and consider deferring migration to hotfix.
- Dedicated pool quota update (INF-330) not confirmed (Olivia) - medium-high. Without it, promo may be rate-limited; contingency: extend canary window and stagger promo.

Canary plan snapshot:
- Start: Mon 04:00 UTC (1% traffic) -> 24h -> increase to 10% if health stable -> 48h at 10% -> decide promo.
- Metrics to watch: p95 latency (tokens/sec), error rate (5xx), kv cache hit ratio, cost per 1k tokens.
- Canary SLO gates: p95 within +10% of baseline, error rate <0.5% absolute increase, no critical alerts for 60m.

Quick notes / reminders to self:
- Remind QA to include throughput test with long context (8k tokens) in nightly run.
- Confirm that function-calling changes in PR #187 are backward-compatible with existing client SDKs. Linked PR above.
- Ask Product to confirm user-facing changelog copy by Fri morning.

Action items (owner - due)
- Evan Ramirez - validate REL-452 in staging and post results to thread (due: 2026-03-05 12:00 UTC)
- Olivia Martin - confirm dedicated pool quota update and publish numbers (due: 2026-03-05 EOD)
- Maya Singh - kick off canary deploy dry-run in staging and attach logs (due: 2026-03-04 18:00 UTC)
- Samir Patel - run perf baselines tonight and share summary (due: 2026-03-04 23:00 UTC)
- Luke Wu (me) - update runbook with rollback thresholds and link pager duty play (due: 2026-03-05 09:00 UTC)
- Release Engineer (TBD) - run automated rollback dry-run in staging and report (due: 2026-03-05 15:00 UTC)

Open questions / discussion items for the meeting:
- If migration REL-452 is risky, do we split migration from code release? Pros/cons quick list.
- Can we extend canary window without impacting customers? Ops costs to confirm.

Notes to self: keep meeting focused - surface only blockers and decisions. Avoid deep dive on lower-priority tech debt. Capture owners inline for faster follow-up.

References / links (for meeting doc):
- Jira REL-452 (migration)
- Jira INF-330 (dedicated pool quotas)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/release-engine/pull/187 (function-calling changes)
- Confluence: Launch readiness checklist (linked_artifacts above)

End of prep note. Will tidy after sync and move to in_review once blockers resolved.
